instrument_name: 2026 Act No. 110 (H.4216, R117): amends 12-6-510(C) rates, 12-6-50, 12-6-1140(15) SCIAD, 12-6-1720, 12-6-3632; Section 6 orders DOR to adjust withholding tables
figure_or_rule_carried: In force: tax years beginning after 2025: 0-30,000 taxable income 1.99%; 30,000+ 5.21% minus 966 (brackets indexed per 12-6-520). From TY2027 top rate falls further if revenue projected +5% (BEA trigger) until 1.99%. Federal standard/itemized deduction no longer adopted; new SC Income Adjusted Deduction 15,000 single/MFS, 22,500 HoH, 30,000 MFJ, phased out over FAGI 40,000/55,000, 60,000/82,500, 80,000/110,000. SC EITC capped at 200. Section 6: DOR shall adjust withholding tables. Operating level: annual assessment (return); withholding changes only when DOR reissues tables.

As of 2026-11-02 the page still links the 2026 tables WH1603_2026 (Rev. 10/30/25) and formula WH1603F_2026 (Rev. 11/4/25, md5 identical to the 2026-10-29 copy): no post-Act-110 withholding revision published. Wages taxed where earned; SC resident working in a no-income-tax state -> SC withholding. E-file/pay required at 15,000+ per quarter or 24+ payments/yr (MyDORWAY). WH-1605 Q1-Q3, WH-1606 Q4/annual; due Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31. Payments: resident agents same frequency as federal deposits; nonresident agents quarterly if <500/quarter, monthly by 15th if >=500. Payments allocated by paycheck date. W-2/1099 upload on MyDORWAY.

instrument_name: SC W-4 (2026) Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate, Rev. 12/5/25
figure_or_rule_carried: Fields: name, address, SSN, status Single/Married/Married-withhold-at-Single, allowances (line 5), additional amount (line 6), exempt (line 7; expires 2026-12-31), military spouse domicile election (RR #24-5); employer boxes 8-10 (name/address, first date of employment, FEIN). Regular wages: withholding based on allowances, may not be a flat amount or percentage. New hires reported within 20 days (SC Code 43-5-598, newhire.sc.gov); rehire after 60+ days separation = new hire. All employers with SC wages/withholding must submit W-2s directly to SCDOR (SSA filing does not satisfy).
Wage-bracket tables 0-10 allowances by period; daily table top line: over 364 = amount shown plus 6.0% of excess. Still the edition linked 2026-11-02 (pre-Act 110 rates 0/3/6%).

instrument_name: SCDOR Information Letter #26-20, Individual Income Tax Reform (Act 110 of 2026)
article_or_section: 4 pp.: Tax Brackets and Rates; SCIAD; EITC; Filing Requirements; Withholding Tables
figure_or_rule_carried: Confirms Act 110: 2026 schedule 0-29,999 1.99%; 30,000+ 5.21% minus 966; brackets CPI-indexed (12-6-520); from TY2027 top rate cut if BEA projects +5% revenue; SC taxable income starts from federal AGI from TY2026; SCIAD 15,000 S/MFS (phase-out AGI 40,000-95,000), 22,500 HoH (60,000-142,500), 30,000 MFJ (80,000-190,000), reduction rounded down to 10; nonresident SCIAD prorated SC AGI/federal AGI; EITC 125% of federal capped 200. Withholding: 'The SCDOR will consult with RFA to adjust the withholding tables' - no date and no new table given. Operating level: assessment (annual return); withholding unchanged until DOR republishes.

instrument_name: SC DEW SUITS Wage Report and Payment File Specification, version 1.6 (10.25.2023)
authority: South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce
article_or_section: 91 pp.: 1.1 scope; 2 ICESA layouts (A, E, S, T, F); 4 EFW2 layouts (RA, RE, RW, RT...); XML and CSV; appendices (SSN validation 12.6, error messages 12.7)
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI wage and tax report filed in SUITS by direct entry, copy from prior quarter, no-wage report, or upload in ICESA, EFW2, XML or CSV; amendments via Amend Prior Report; agents file for clients with POA on file. RW record: SSN 9 digits without hyphens (999999999 if unavailable), names as on SSN card. Linked from the DEW UI Tax Forms page (wayback 2026-10-09). Direct GET to dew.sc.gov returns 403; file retrieved from wayback 2025-08-04 capture.

instrument_name: SC Code of Regulations Chapter 47 (Department of Employment and Workforce): 47-1, 47-7, 47-14, 47-15, 47-16, 47-19
authority: SC Legislative Services Agency (Code of Regulations)
article_or_section: 47-1 cash value in kind; 47-7 interest surcharge; 47-14 records 5 years; 47-15(C) quarterly wage report; 47-16 contributions due; 47-19 separation notices and mass separations
figure_or_rule_carried: 47-15(C): each employer submits on or before the last day of the first month after the quarter a report listing each individual employed: employer name and DEW account number, worker full name, SSN, total wages paid in the quarter, other info per form. 47-16: contributions payable quarterly, due last day of month following the quarter (extension up to 15 days on application). 47-14: UI records kept 5 years (pay period dates, name, SSN, hours if less than full time, wages incl. special payments, cash value of in-kind pay, hire/rehire/separation date and reason). 47-19: no employer-issued separation notice at termination; employer answers DEW's notice of claim per 41-31-160; mass separation (10+ workers, same establishment/time/reason) -> Form UCB-113 per worker within 10 days (excl. Sundays/holidays). 47-1: board/lodging valued for UI contributions at DEW rates. 47-7: interest surcharge shown with DACA on rate notice.

instrument_name: SC Consumer Protection Code 37-5-104 (no garnishment) and 37-5-106 (no discharge)
figure_or_rule_carried: 37-5-104: for a debt arising from a consumer credit sale, consumer lease, consumer loan or consumer rental-purchase agreement, the creditor may not attach unpaid earnings by garnishment or like proceedings (regardless of where made). 37-5-106: no discharge because a creditor subjected or attempted to subject earnings to garnishment for such a judgment. Payroll consequence: consumer-debt wage garnishment orders are not available under SC law; support orders, federal (IRS, student loan AWG) and state tax levies follow their own statutes.

instrument_name: SC Financial Identity Fraud and Identity Theft Protection Act 37-20-180 (SSN restrictions)
figure_or_rule_carried: A person may not: publicly display an SSN or any portion of 6+ digits; print it on access cards; require it over the Internet without secure connection/encryption; print an SSN or 6+ digit portion on materials mailed to the individual unless state or federal law requires it; disclose to third parties without written consent except legitimate business/government purpose. Mailed SSN (where permitted) may not be on a postcard or visible through the envelope. Payroll consequence: mailed pay statements show at most 5 digits of the SSN (W-2 is required by federal law).

instrument_name: SC Code Title 63 ch. 17 child support income withholding: 63-17-1210, 63-17-1460, 63-17-3520, 63-17-3530
figure_or_rule_carried: 63-17-1460: payor starts deduction no later than the next regular pay period after service; total withholding capped at CCPA 15 USC 1673(b); employer fee up to 3 USD per withholding instance deducted from obligor income (unless waived); multiple notices: comply up to CCPA limit, priority to current support, no order left unimplemented; remit to the State Disbursement Unit within 7 working days of withholding, stating the withholding date; on termination, within 20 days return the notice and inform the clerk of the termination date and final paycheck. 63-17-3520/3530: out-of-state IWO treated as SC order; fee, maximum, timing and priorities follow the law of the obligor's principal place of employment. 63-17-1210: DSS CSED new-hire program (rehire after layoff/leave counts; fields name, address, SSN, DOB, salary, employer name/address/FEIN).

instrument_name: SC Code 43-5-598 State Directory of New Hires (mandatory reporting)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer hiring an employee who resides or works in SC reports to the state directory of new hires (DSS) within 20 calendar days of hire; electronic transmitters semi-monthly, 12-16 days apart. Fields: employer name, address, FEIN; employee name, address, SSN. New hire includes rehire after separation/layoff/furlough/unpaid leave of at least 60 consecutive days. Date of hire = first day of work for which compensation is due. Multistate employers transmitting electronically may designate one state (per federal rule). Portal newhire.sc.gov (direct GET fails; wayback 2026-10-16 shell page only).

instrument_name: SC Code 6-1-130 local minimum wage preemption
figure_or_rule_carried: A political subdivision (municipality, county, school district, special purpose or public service district) may not establish, mandate or require a minimum wage above the FLSA section 6 federal rate (29 USC 206), nor a minimum wage for FLSA-exempt wages; it may set wage rates in its own contracts. SC has no state minimum-wage statute: the applicable minimum is the federal 7.25 USD/h (FLSA). Therefore no local minimum wages exist in SC.

instrument_name: SC Code 41-1-25 employee-benefit mandates by political subdivisions prohibited (2017 Act No. 3, S.218); 41-1-70 jury/subpoena
figure_or_rule_carried: 41-1-25: no political subdivision may establish, mandate or require any employee benefit (health, disability, death, AD&D, paid holidays, paid sick leave, paid vacation, paid personal leave, retirement, profit sharing), except for its own employees. SC chapter 41-1 contains no private-sector paid sick leave or vacation mandate; therefore no state or local paid sick leave applies. 41-1-70: dismissal/demotion for jury service or subpoena compliance actionable (no paid jury leave mandate). 41-1-130: break time to express breast milk (see text).

instrument_name: SC Code Title 41 ch. 27 (Employment Security Law definitions): 41-27-260, 41-27-265, 41-27-380, 41-27-410
article_or_section: 41-27-260 exempted employment; 41-27-265 corporate officers; 41-27-380(A)-(B) wages and taxable wage base; 41-27-410 DACA
figure_or_rule_carried: 41-27-380(B): UI taxable wage base 14,000 USD per employee per calendar year from 2015-01-01 (statutory; not indexed; wages paid under other states' UI laws count toward it). 41-27-380(A): wages include commissions, bonuses, back-pay awards, cash value of in-kind pay, and all reported tips; exclude employer plan payments for retirement, sickness/accident disability, medical, death (no cash option); National Guard/reserve drill pay; employer-paid FICA for agricultural/domestic workers; post-65 payments when no work; in-kind pay to agricultural/domestic workers. 41-27-410: DACA 0.06% of wages for all contributory employers except reimbursing and governmental employers. 41-27-260 exclusions: seafood industry labour; casual labour outside trade; family employment (spouse, child, child under 18 of parent); federal employment; elected/policymaking public posts; churches and ministers; students employed by own school; student nurses/interns; newspaper delivery under 18; commission-only insurance and real-estate agents; direct sellers; owner-operator drivers; agricultural labour by students/part-time. 41-27-265: corporate officers covered unless the corporation elects out in writing for at least 2 years and notifies officers.

In force from 2026-07-01: benefit ratio look-back 12 quarters through tax year 2026, 16 quarters for tax year 2027, 20 quarters from 2028 (rate class 1 employers in 2026 keep the 12-quarter calculation until they leave class 1); solvency surcharge section 41-31-45 rewritten (surcharge applies in each year the trust fund reserve is below the solvency target as of June 30); 41-31-60: delinquent report on computation date -> class 20 rate; tax execution issued on/after 2027-01-01 unpaid -> employer rate plus 2 percentage points (pre-2027 executions -> class 20); 41-31-350 late report penalty 10% of contributions due, minimum 25 USD (1,000 cap removed); 41-31-370 interest 1% per month, 10% penalty if unpaid 10 days after assessment (1,000 cap removed). Same local file as US-SC-002 (code page current at 2026-10-29).

W-2s due to employees, IRS/SSA and SCDOR by January 31. Methods: EFW2 .txt upload (SSA Pub. 42-007; zip if over 25 MB; must include the SC RS state record; the file sent to SSA can be reused if it carries the state record), Excel template (up to 30 employees), manual entry. W-2c via EFW2C (SSA 42-014); W-2G/1099 via IRS Pub. 1220. Corrections: cancel and resubmit same business day; later via Withholding section. One file may hold several businesses (accepted/rejected whole).

instrument_name: SCDOR RS-1 W-2 and 1099 Filing Instructions and Specifications, Tax Year 2025 (October 2025)
article_or_section: 15 pp.: SC requirements; WH-1612 transmittal; Code RS state record specification pp. 8-12; common errors; Appendix A
figure_or_rule_carried: EFW2 records required by SC: RA, RE, RW, RS (state record, required by SC though not federally), RT, RF; RO/RU/RV optional. RS: positions 1-2 'RS'; 3-4 state numeric code 45; 5-9 blank; 10-18 full SSN (no truncation, zeros if unavailable); names as on SSN card; state employer account number; state taxable wages and state income tax withheld fields (positions per p.10-12); supplemental data 1/2 at 338-412 / 413-487; record length 512 + CR/LF. Truncated SSNs rejected. Electronic filing mandatory at 10 or more W-2/1099 forms per year (or the lower IRS threshold); paper filers send transmittal WH-1612. Edition covers TY2025 (filed by 2026-01-31); the TY2026 edition (filing January 2027) was not published at 2026-11-02 (same URL).

instrument_name: SC Code Title 12 ch. 8 Income Tax Withholding (local copy 2026-11-02): 12-8-10, 12-8-510, 12-8-520, 12-8-1520
figure_or_rule_carried: Local copy of the chapter read for US-SCR3-001 (that row has no local file). Employee = resident receiving wages wherever services are rendered + nonresident receiving wages for services in SC. Withhold when wages expected to reach 1,000 in the year, using DOR tables/rules; nearest-dollar computation allowed. 12-8-520(C)(1): resident wages earned in another state not subject to SC withholding if subject to that state's withholding. 12-8-1520: resident withholding agents remit SC tax on or before their federal deposit due dates; agents not depositing federally and nonresident agents: by the 15th of the next month when 500+ withheld in a month, else by the last day of the month after the quarter; 24+ payments a year -> electronic (12-54-250). No 2026 amendment to chapter 8 in the history notes (checked mechanically).
